types.name: FAudioCurve
types.doc:
Sampler for the author-editable attenuation curves carried on
AudioSourceComponent. A curve is a small sorted set of {distance, value}
keys; the engine evaluates gain-over-distance and cutoff-over-distance from
these each frame when the source is spatialized. Keys are authored in
arbitrary order — the evaluator sorts a local copy before sampling — and the
curve is flat-clamped outside its first and last key.

members.name: Evaluate
members.signature: static float Evaluate(const std::vector<FAudioCurveKey>& keys, float distance, EAudioCurveInterp interp, float emptyValue = 1.0f)
members.doc:
Sample the curve at `distance`. Empty curves return `emptyValue` so a
caller can fold the result into a multiply without a branch. Linear does
straight lerp between the bracketing keys; Cubic uses a Catmull-Rom
spline across the neighbouring keys (clamped at the ends) for a smoother
rolloff that still passes through every authored key.

types.name: AudioEffectType
types.doc:
Built-in DSP effect types. Filters (LowPass..HighShelf) + Delay wrap
miniaudio nodes directly. Reverb (simplified Freeverb) and Compressor
(feedforward peak detector) are custom ma_node subclasses living in
AudioEffect.cpp — miniaudio doesn't ship those out of the box.

types.name: AudioEffect
types.doc:
Base for every DSP node we put on a bus. Owns one ma_node*-shaped object —
derived classes pick which `ma_*_node` they wrap and how to interpret their
config. Lifetime: created via the AudioEngine::CreateXxxEffect factories
(which need engine init), destroyed by `~AudioEffect` after the engine has
detached the node from the graph.

**Threading**: parameter mutators (e.g. SetCutoff) run on the game thread but
the reinit they need is not safe against the audio thread reading the same
coefficients. So a mutator only *publishes* the new values; the audio thread
applies them between blocks, from the engine's process callback. Bypass uses
`ma_node_set_state`, which is lock-safe and needs none of this.

envelope detection is linked (envelope = max across channels) so stereo

ratio      : 1..30     (1 = no compression, ∞ = limiter)
attackMs   : 0.1..200
releaseMs  : 5..2000
kneeDb     : 0..30     (soft knee width; 0 = hard knee)
makeupDb   : 0..24     (post-compression gain)

members.doc:
Per-bus effect chain. Insertion appends to the end of the chain (bus →
existing chain → new effect → endpoint). Removal pulls the effect out
and re-wires neighbours. The Ref ownership keeps the effect alive while
attached — caller may drop their own Ref after AddBusEffect.

**Threading**: chain mutation must happen on the main thread. miniaudio's
node attach/detach is internally lock-safe but the chain bookkeeping
(m_busEffects vector) is not.

members.doc:
Bridge surface for languages without RefCounted semantics. RegisterManaged
takes ownership of a Ref and returns a stable raw pointer a host
language can hold. The raw pointer stays valid until DestroyManaged is
called (which also detaches the effect from any bus chain it's in).

Lifetime overlap with the bus chain: AddBusEffect bumps the ref count
(the chain holds its own Ref), so a "managed" effect can be in both
m_managedEffects AND m_busEffects[bus] simultaneously without leaking.

members.name: RegisterVoice
members.doc:
Every AudioSource registers a voice on Load and drops it on Unload, so
the engine has the live-sound list miniaudio does not expose. The budget
pass (UpdateVoices, driven by AudioSystem each tick) ranks the playing
voices and keeps only the top `audio.max_voices` audible; the rest are
VIRTUALIZED — their ma_sound is stopped so it costs no mixer time, while
the engine keeps advancing a wall-clock playback position. A voice that
wins its slot back seeks to that position and resumes.

Score = priority (0..100, per-source, dominates) + effective volume
(0..1, base volume × distance attenuation to listener 0, tie-breaks).
Audible voices carry a hysteresis bonus when ranked, so a voice sitting
on the budget boundary does not flip audible/virtual frame to frame.

These are the AudioSource↔engine plumbing calls — gameplay code drives
AudioSource, not this.

types.name: FAudioImpulseMemory
types.doc:
FAudioImpulseMemory — the ambience's short memory of loud things: where the
recent impulses (a scan, a door slam, a gunshot) happened and how much of
each is still "in the air". Two things read it:

- the crackle accumulator: the decayed sum of every impulse, squashed to
0..1 and published as the "Crackle" parameter each tick, so a bed of
crackles thickens after a burst of noise and thins out again;
- spatial queries: how much happened near a point recently, and where the
latest impulses were, so an ambience can answer from the direction the
noise came from rather than from everywhere at once.

Each impulse halves every HalfLife seconds and is forgotten below 1% of its
strength or past the capacity (oldest first). Main thread only; ticked by
AudioEngine::UpdateVoices.

types.doc:
One binding: a named parameter read through a curve onto a target. The curve
keys are {parameter value, target value} — FAudioCurveKey's `distance` field
carries the parameter value. EAudioCurveInterp::Step turns the curve into
bands, so a parameter crossing a range boundary jumps to the next band.

types.name: FAudioParameters
types.doc:
FAudioParameters — the RTPC layer: named, game-set values ("Attention",
"Heat", "ScanRange") that sounds read instead of being driven one by one.
A value set here glides to its target over the parameter's smoothing time,
so a jumpy gameplay value does not zipper the mix. Sources bind through
AudioSource::AddParameterBinding (or the AudioSourceComponent modulation
fields), submixes through BindSubmix, MetaSound control inputs through
MetaSoundComponent::parameterLinks; AudioEngine::UpdateVoices advances the
glide and applies every binding once a tick.

Main thread only, like the rest of the mixer's control surface.

and pitch multiply the authored values; the cutoff sits under occlusion.

key instead of gliding between them. Applied when the source is created.

types.doc:
An opening between two rooms that sound travels through: a doorway, a
hatch, a vent, a door with how far it stands open. The opening lies in the
entity's local XY plane (Width along X, Height along Y) and the rooms it
joins are found by probing Probe Depth along its local Z on either side —
or named outright with Room A / Room B.

the material table's: this is where a heavy fire door that is quieter than
its wood suggests says so. A partly open door mixes the two states by
energy — a crack lets through far more than its fraction of the area would
suggest in dB, which is what an ajar door sounds like.

types.name: FConvolutionEngine
types.doc:

convolution reverb. The impulse response is split into blockSize
partitions, each FFT'd once at Init; per input block one FFT + P complex

types.name: FEchoTail
types.doc:
FEchoTail — the echo a space gives back, built from where the scanner's rays
actually landed instead of a reverb preset per room. Every shot contributes
its hit distances to a decaying histogram (0.5 m bins out to 64 m) and its
misses to an "open air" weight. From that:

- pre-delay = 2 * nearest well-populated distance / c;
- decay (RT60) = the mean-free-path law with a fixed wall absorption,
RT60 = 0.113 * meanDistance, shortened as more rays escape;
- density = returned rays / all rays.

The estimate is published as the EchoDecay / EchoPreDelay / EchoDensity
parameters, and BuildImpulseResponse synthesises a stereo IR from the same
histogram — one early reflection per populated bin at its round-trip time,
then a decorrelated noise tail decaying at the RT60. With a target submix set
(SetTargetSubmix, or the audio.EchoTailSubmix cvar) a convolution reverb on
that submix is rebuilt from the IR whenever the estimate moves enough, at
most once a second. Main thread only; ticked by AudioEngine::UpdateVoices.

types.name: FGeometricAcoustics
types.doc:
FGeometricAcoustics — sound worked out from the level's geometry. Three
answers, all deterministic for a given seed so two machines agree:

- Occlusion: every wall a straight line from source to listener crosses,
each costing what FSoundOcclusion's material table says. Once a scan
hierarchy is installed for a world, FSoundPropagation::Evaluate takes
its direct path from here — so world sources, proximity voice, radio
speakers and AI hearing are all blocked by the scanned walls.
- Reverb: rays from the listener bounce off the surfaces (specular or
scattered by the material), and the decay follows Eyring's law from the
traced mean free path and the energy-weighted absorption, rays that
escape counting as open air.
- Early reflections: exact image sources. Planes are discovered by rays
from both ends, mirrored up to the reflection order, and every path is
confirmed against the geometry — the wall is really there at the
bounce point and nothing blocks any leg.

Echolocation is the same machinery pointed outward: a click, and what each
ray's surface sends back toward the emitter and when.

types.name: FSoundOcclusionMaterial
types.doc:
FSoundOcclusion — the one occlusion law every sound in the engine obeys:
world sources, proximity voice, radio speakers and AI hearing all ask it.
Before it there were three, with their own constants, and a comment in the
voice code claiming they agreed. They did not, which is exactly how a player
ends up hearing a friend through a door the creature on the other side of it
cannot — the one thing the co-op design cannot afford.

The law is keyed by the MATERIAL a ray crosses, not by a per-source knob:
every hit resolves an ESurfaceType already (footsteps pick their cue from
it), so a level authored for footsteps is authored for occlusion too. A thin
partition costs -9 dB and pulls the low-pass to 2.5 kHz, a thick wall -18 dB
and 900 Hz. Several walls along one ray SUM in dB and take the darkest
cutoff — filtering alone would leave a blocked source as loud as an open
one, which is the giveaway that the wall is not really there.

The table lives in data: Config/Engine.ini under audio.occlusion.<Surface>
(db, cutoff_hz), editable on Project Settings > Audio. A portal (a door, a
hatch) is the place for an authored exception, not the material table.

types.name: FSoundRoom
types.doc:
FSoundPropagation — rooms joined by portals, and the one answer to "how does
a sound get from here to there". World sources, proximity voice, radio
speakers and AI hearing all ask Evaluate; that the creature and the player
get the same answer through the same door is the point of it.

The answer is the LOUDER of two routes. Straight through the walls is
FSoundOcclusion's material trace. Round through the openings is the chain of
portals from the source's room to the listener's, each portal adding its own
authored loss and cutoff, plus what the detour costs in spreading
(20·log10 of path length over straight distance). Between two rooms a
straight line that hits no collision either runs out through an opening —
and costs what that opening costs — or it crosses the author's room
boundary where the level has no collision yet (a greybox), which counts as
one thick wall: an author who drew two rooms meant them apart. Two rooms
with no chain of portals at all are sealed and hear each other only through
the walls.

Rooms and portals are built from RoomVolumeComponent / PortalComponent every
tick by FSoundPropagationSystem — a door that swings changes the next query.
Where no system runs, Evaluate falls back to the material trace alone.
